_comment: TARGET-tier scope definition for a WRAP-ONLY campaign over libxml2
v2.15.3. There is no port scope: nothing is translated to native Rust.
The deliverable is a safe Rust wrapper over the whole published C API,
so the target is defined by the headers that publish it.
_comment_files: A WRAP campaign: `files.import` names the API to wrap, and there is no
target. The two keys are mutually exclusive - `target` names what this
target OWNS (imports are then derived from it), `import` names an API to
wrap (nothing is owned).
Seeding off the public headers is what makes this expressible. Entity
classification is DEFINITION-anchored, so naming these headers under
`files.target` would admit only what they DEFINE - inline functions,
macros, value structs - and drop every function they merely DECLARE, whose
body sits in a root .c. As an IMPORT seed the test is declaration-site
membership instead, which is the right question for a public header: the
bodies live in files this campaign does not own, and 'does target code
reach it' has no answer when there is no target code.
Consequences that fall out, with no objective flag anywhere: a struct
DEFINED in one of these headers keeps its full field layout (its fields
are the API), one merely forward-declared stays an opaque handle, symbols
order on their signatures rather than their bodies, and --transitive over
an opaque type pulls nothing it does not need.
Ownership analysis is unaffected: ptr_args/ptr_ret come from the T2
tables, which cover the whole database regardless of scope, so the real
bodies are still what free/store behaviour is read from.
45 headers, 1416 XMLPUBFUN declarations at this tag.
_comment_out_of_scope: `paths` is empty: `files.import` names only include/libxml/, so the test
harness, fuzzers, Python bindings and examples are outside it by
`features` is documentation only - no composer reads it. It lists the
LIBXML2_WITH_* options OFF in the configure line recorded in build.json.
